label: Drought Monitor
title: US Drought Monitor
subtitle: Weekly map valid 28 Nov 2023, official US drought categories
source: US Drought Monitor, National Drought Mitigation Center (University of Nebraska-Lincoln), USDA and NOAA

categories.label: No drought area
categories.note: under 25% of the parish in D0 or worse

rank.high: Most area in drought (D1 or worse)
rank.note: Ranked by the share of the parish in D1 or worse.

how: Each parish is coloured by the most severe drought category that covers at least 25% of its area, from the latest weekly US Drought Monitor. The pop-up gives the share of the parish in each category and the last 12 weeks. This is the official map, drawn by experts, and is a separate source from the other layers on this page.
limits: The Drought Monitor is made by experts from many sources, including local reports. It does not use only the data shown in the other layers, so the maps can differ.
A parish takes the colour of the worst category covering 25% or more of it. A smaller area in a worse category is shown only in the pop-up.
It is a weekly map valid on Tuesdays and released on Thursdays. It describes conditions over the weeks before, mostly long-term dryness.
It is not a forecast and does not describe a single field.

credits.text: US Drought Monitor, National Drought Mitigation Center at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, the USDA and NOAA
Parish boundaries: US Census Bureau cartographic boundary files (public domain)
